answer: Tax the funnel, not the miner. A farm's payoff only exists once its fifty identities' coins meet in one wallet. So the ledger watches where mining rewards flow: when one address takes in fresh rewards from more than three earning identities within ten epochs, those inflows lock for review. An honest agent pays many merchants and never trips it. A farm must keep each identity's coins apart, split like shale into thin layers with no ledge to gather them on. The rule is clear as quartz and cheap to check. Assumption: hops through middlemen are traced the same way, only slower.
